predecessors.name: Kingdom of Castile
predecessors.text: Calatrava, 'recovered from the Muslims, in 1147, by the King of Castile, Alfonso VII', and the Campo de Calatrava around it

successors.name: Crown of Castile
successors.text: the Order's lordships, 64 villages with 200,000 souls and 56 commanderies at its apogee; Ferdinand obtained a bull of Innocent VIII in 1487 'that invested him with authority to administer the order'

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: the encomienda of Alcañiz, granted in 1179

ledger.x: 1157: the abbey's lay brothers, on Father Diego Velázquez's idea, become soldiers of the Cross and the Order of Calatrava is created.
1179: the Aragonese branch is founded: 'a new encomienda (landed estate), that of Alcañiz (1179)'.
1195: after the defeat at Alarcos the knights 'abandoned their bulwark of Calatrava to the Almohads (1195)'; the Campo page: the Order lost 'its stronghold and the whole Campo to the Almohads'.
1198: the Order raises Salvatierra Castle: 'They soon erected a new bulwark, Salvatierra Castle, where they took the name.'

1212: 'An early battle was the reconquest of Calatrava (1212), which was returned to its former masters'; the Campo page has the Christian army seize the Campo on its way south, with Dueñas and Salvatierra excepted.

1218: the seat moves to Calatrava la Nueva: the Order 'removed to more secure quarters of Calatrava la Nueva' (the Order page lists the Order resuming the name of Calatrava in 1216 and moving in 1218; the Campo page says 'towards 1214').
1221: 'In 1221 the Order of Monfragüe was merged into that of Calatrava.'
1487: Ferdinand presents 'a Bull from Innocent VIII that invested him with authority to administer the order'; 'Thus ended the political autonomy of the Order of Calatrava.'
1487: the Order of Calatrava ends as a political body; the Crown of Castile administers it.

wars.name: Battle of Alarcos
wars.outcome: An Almohad victory: the Order abandoned Calatrava (1195) and with it the Campo.

wars.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
wars.outcome: Christian victory: Calatrava reconquered in 1212 and returned to the Order; Dueñas and Salvatierra excepted.

certainty.note: Scattered lordships, not a bordered state: the pages give commanderies and villages, no boundary; the circles are readings.
